title: Sombi, Senegalese Coconut Rice Pudding
author: SAVEUR Editors
desc: Four cups of coconut milk with shredded coconut, brown sugar, salt and a vanilla bean reduced slightly, then two cups of cooked rice that break down and thicken it — ‘more like a creamy porridge than a pudding’.
longDesc: The 2012 Saveur printing. Coconut milk, unsweetened shredded coconut, packed brown sugar, salt and a vanilla bean with its seeds are brought to a boil in a 4-quart saucepan over medium heat and cooked, stirring often, about 5 minutes until reduced slightly. Cooked white rice goes in and cooks, stirring, about 5 minutes until it breaks down and thickens the mixture slightly. Off the heat, fresh lime juice is stirred in, and it is served hot. The headnote calls it ‘more like a creamy porridge than a pudding’, eaten for breakfast or as an afternoon snack in Senegal.
ingredients: 1 cup unsweetened shredded coconut, fresh or dried
1/2 cup packed light or dark brown sugar
1 vanilla bean, seeds scraped and reserved
steps: Bring the coconut milk, coconut, sugar, salt and the vanilla bean with its seeds to a boil in a 4-quart saucepan over medium heat and cook, stirring often, until reduced slightly, about 5 minutes.
Add the rice and cook, stirring, until the rice breaks down and thickens the mixture slightly, about 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat, stir in the lime juice and serve hot.
chefTips: Two printed cues: ‘reduced slightly’ and ‘until rice breaks down and thickens’.
It is deliberately porridge-like, not set.
Lime is added off the heat.
commonMistakes: Boiling hard, which can split the coconut milk.
Over-reducing before the rice goes in.
Adding lime while on the boil.
reheating: Warm with a splash of coconut milk.
healthBenefits: Coconut milk is rich in saturated fat.
A sweet dish — a breakfast or snack in moderation.
culturalNote: SAVEUR’s headnote: ‘More like a creamy porridge than a pudding in consistency, this sweet dish is commonly eaten for breakfast or as an afternoon snack in Senegal.’ Published 30 May 2012.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Sombi (Senegalese Coconut Rice Pudding)’ / ‘Senegal Coconut Rice Pudding’. Byline as printed: ‘SAVEUR Editors’ (a staff byline; the 2012 gallery index shows no byline for this item — both recorded). Publication: Saveur. Date: ‘Published on May 30, 2012’. Yield: ‘Serves 4-6’. TWO-PASS, identical.
The page prints the fraction glyph ‘1⁄2’ (fraction slash). Cues in fragments: ‘until reduced slightly, about 5 minutes’; ‘until rice breaks down and thickens soup slightly, about 5 minutes’.

UNRECONCILED with SEN083 (Thiam: 2 cups coconut milk, 1 cup cooked rice, white sugar, honey-glazed mango) and SEN085 (no coconut at all): this one uses 4 cups coconut milk, 2 cups cooked rice, brown sugar, no mango.
